comments.author: @babajaiy8246
comments.text:
Sorry Geoff, what you're saying is just BS. In areas like the Canadian shield where it is rock, you don't need to do all that digging, you just build on top. And there are small cities and towns that do that in the Canadian Shield. In other words, just build differently.
Building on 'solid' rock has it's advantages too - California builds in earthquake zones, and has to spend extra on building to accommodate those risks. In the Canadian shield you don't have to spend as much - You have a rock solid foundation for buildings to start with - You don't have to spend money on a foundation in other words - You already have it ( and it's free ). That's a cost savings actually.

You get the fur trade right in terms of the large role it played but got it wrong saying the Hudson's Bay "Could not establish much of a presence in the region" - That is nonsense too. The HBC was not about establishing a presence - It was about extracting resources, in this case fur, and they did that - only needing outposts and nothing much more for it. The expanding more west was not because their activities in the Canadian Shield was insufficient, but rather it was just the natural outcome of a company to want to grow and expand.

In other words, contrary to what you say  "....they couldn't make it work....there must be something wrong with the area..." is completely wrong, because they did make it work.

But the real reason for Canada's population being where it mostly resides is because of the 'evolution' of the fur trade in Canada through time and Canada's close association with Britain. 

Economically wise Canada became a resource country - with very little effort to grow in terms of 'added' value to it's resources for export.

With such a type of economy mainly this meant those traditional areas of settlement pretty much stayed the main areas of development. 

There never was an incentive or need to expand outside of the traditional areas.

In other words, there's actually much more usable land than you think or imply in your video.

You simply really don't understand Canada and it's history like you think you do.
